title: USGS geological context
publication: Tanaka et al. (2014), Geologic map of Mars, USGS SIM 3292
coordinateReference: GCS_Mars_2000_Sphere (ArcGIS 104971), radius 3396190 m; spherical latitude and east-positive longitude in degrees. Source Robinson geometry transformed by the service.
processing: Regional intersect queries in 104971; maximum allowable offset 0.001 degrees (about 59 m at equator); even/odd polygon holes retained; clipped to declared bounds. Simplification tolerance is not positional accuracy.
limitation: Regional geological interpretation. Too coarse to distinguish local outcrops or determine footing, bearing strength, or exact contact positions. Unit colors are the published service palette. No geological routing penalties are applied.

units.name: Hesperian transition undivided unit
units.characteristics: Irregular plateaus hundreds of kilometers across. Layered. Hundreds of meters to kilometers thick. (lat –6.41° N., long 156.42° E; lat –6.17° N., long 286.05° E.; localities 26, 28)
units.interpretation: Fine-grained eolian sediments and (or) pyroclastic air-fall deposits. Modified by fluvial dissection and eolian erosion. Linear ridges and grooves form yardangs. Tectonically contracted. Channels mostly inverted. Altered by acidic weathering in places

units.name: Amazonian and Hesperian impact unit
units.characteristics: Craters with rims and surrounding blankets; some include single to multi-lobed blanket forms, dense secondary crater chains, and (or) central peak or pit. Blanket thicknesses of meters to a few hundred meters. (lat 23.17° N., long 207.77° E.
units.interpretation: Upturned, ejected, and brecciated target rocks and sediments, with local areas of impact melt. Post-impact mass-wasting and fluvial-lacustrine and eolian infill of craters common

units.name: Hesperian and Noachian transition unit
units.characteristics: Knobs, mesas, and intervening aprons and plains. May be tens to hundreds of meters thick. (lat 10.96° N., long 111.71° E.; locality 18)
units.interpretation: Noachian impact breccias, sediments, and volcanic deposits with intervening aprons of Hesperian mass-wasted materials. Tectonically contracted

units.name: Early Hesperian transition unit
units.characteristics: Plains-forming deposits, undulating to moderately rugged; includes scattered low knobs and mesas of Noachian highland material. May be tens to hundreds of meters thick. (lat 13.38° N., long 116.70° E.; localities 2, 16)
units.interpretation: Mass-wasting, fluvial/lacustrine, and other sedimentary materials and possibly volcanic rocks in places. Tectonically contracted

units.name: Middle Noachian highland unit
units.characteristics: Uneven to rolling topography; high-relief outcrops that extend hundreds to thousands of kilometers. Commonly layered in crater walls. May be hundreds of meters to more than a kilometer thick. (lat –47.17° N., long 349.33° E.; localities 7, 14, 19, 20, 22, 23, 31)
units.interpretation: Undifferentiated impact, volcanic, fluvial, and basin materials. Moderately to heavily degraded

units.name: Middle Noachian highland massif unit
units.characteristics: High-relief massifs tens of kilometers across separated by broad linear troughs and valleys. Kilometers thick. (lat –44.48° N., long 307.54° E.)
units.interpretation: Ancient, degraded crustal rocks uplifted by large, basin-forming impacts. Dissected by basin-related fault structures and erosional valleys

units.name: Amazonian and Hesperian impact unit

units.interpretation: Upturned, ejected, and brecciated target rocks and sediments, with local areas of impact melt. Post-impact mass-wasting and fluvial-lacustrine and eolian infill of craters common

units.name: Early Hesperian volcanic unit
units.characteristics: Planar deposits meters to tens of meters thick and tens to hundreds of kilometers across; lobate scarps common. Variable daytime IR brightness in places. Hundreds of meters or more total thickness. (lat –25.34° N., long 279.97° E.; localities 38, 42)
units.interpretation: Flood lavas, undifferentiated, sourced from regional fissure and vent systems. Tectonically contracted

units.characteristics: Plains-forming deposits, relatively smooth; includes small knobs and mesas of Noachian and perhaps younger material. May be tens to hundreds of meters thick. (lat 18.13° N., long 117.11° E.; localities 8, 15)
units.interpretation: Mass-wasting, fluvial/lacustrine, and possibly other sedimentary materials and volcanic rocks in places. Tectonically contracted

targets.name: Rocknest visit area
targets.question: How does wind sort and accumulate loose sand beside rock obstacles?
targets.evidence: NASA describes a windblown sand-and-dust drift at Rocknest; this offers an aeolian-material comparison with bedrock at Yellowknife Bay.
targets.positionNote: NASA/JPL published rover waypoint at this visit area; not an exact contact, scoop or drill location. Planner endpoint snapped to the 5 m grid. The feed does not state a positional error bound or latitude convention; used as spherical Mars latitude, consistent with the prepared map frame.
targets.timeNote: Curiosity visit: Sol 56, 2012. Environmental replay remains Sol 10 and is a separate demonstration scenario.

targets.name: Yellowknife Bay entry
targets.question: What can sedimentary bedrock reveal about ancient water and deposition?
targets.evidence: NASA documents entry into Yellowknife Bay on Sol 125 and later interprets the bay as a former lake-bed setting. This waypoint represents the entry area, not a drill site.
